note: Also a counter for songs: 한 곡, 두 곡.

ex.en: Let's sing just one more song!
What's the title of this song?
I practiced two pieces on the piano.

note: 잠을 자다 = to sleep; 잠이 오다 = to feel sleepy.

ex.en: I couldn't sleep last night.
If I drink coffee, I can't fall asleep.
I almost fell asleep during the meeting.

note: Formal writing also uses it for 'to take' (action, pose).

ex.en: I got really drunk yesterday.
You're already drunk after two beers?
I got a little tipsy at the company dinner.
Please slow down a little.
The internet is really slow.
At this rate, we'll get there by ten.
What time does the bank close?
I withdrew money at the bank.
Is there a bank near here?

en: to be severe, harsh; too much

ex.en: My cold is bad.
That was a bit harsh to say.
Traffic is really bad today.

note: Usually for hardships or problems.

ex.en: I'm going through a hard time these days.
We had a lot of problems when we moved.
I went through the exact same thing.
That restaurant is still delicious.
Is Jisoo still busy?
I took medicine, but my head still hurts.
I completely forgot about the appointment.
My clothes got completely soaked in the rain.
My cold is completely gone now.
What kind of music do you like?
This shop has lots of kinds of bread.
There are so many kinds of vitamins.

note: 이해하다 = to understand; 이해가 안 돼요 = I don't get it.

ex.en: I don't understand this problem.
Thanks for understanding.
Now that I've heard the explanation, I get it.
You just do it like this.
I didn't know it would be this cold today.
I've never had kimchi this good.

en: to turn, spin; to run (a machine)

ex.en: Please run the washing machine.
Can I change the channel?
Don't change the subject.

note: Written 잘못돼요 / 잘못됐어요 (되어 → 돼).

ex.en: I think something went wrong.
The bill is wrong.
The address was wrong, so the package didn't come.

note: 여행하다 = to travel; 여행 가다 = to go on a trip.

ex.en: I'm going on a trip to Jeju next month.
How was your trip?
I like traveling alone.
This bag has a pretty design.
I do design work at my company.
The new app design is easier to use.

note: Usually with a negative: 절대 안 돼요 = absolutely not.

ex.en: Absolutely not.
Don't ever tell anyone this secret.
I'm never late.
I have good news!
Have you heard any news about Jimin lately?
I'll let you know when the results come out.
The child got dressed on her own.
Decide for yourself.
You have to do your homework on your own.

note: Used with ~처럼 or ~ 같다.

ex.en: It's just like a movie.
The two of them are as close as sisters.
It's hot today, just like summer.
I'll take care of that problem.
Did you fix the computer problem?
Let's try to work it out by talking.
Expressing my feelings is hard.
I hid my feelings in the meeting.
Dogs have feelings too.
It's my turn now.
Please line up in order.
Who's next?
I went to the mountains on the weekend.
It's pretty cold up on the mountain.

ex.s: 우리 집 뒤에 작은 산이 있어요.
ex.en: There's a small mountain behind our house.
I need coffee in the morning to get energy.
The kids are full of energy.
I turned off the lights to save energy.
I got flowers for my birthday.
Lots of flowers bloom in spring.
What's this flower called?

en: to hang; to make (a phone call)
note: 전화를 걸다 = to call. ㄹ drops: 거세요, 거는.

ex.en: I'll call you later.
Please hang your coat here.
You have the wrong number.
What does this word mean?
I memorize ten words every day.
I can't think of the word.
The last scene of that movie was the best.
I always cry at this scene.
I took a photo of that scene.
How did your friends react?
I have an allergic reaction to that medicine.
Customers are reacting well to the new menu.

en: to be funny; to make laugh
note: 웃겨요 = it's funny.

ex.en: That video is really funny.
Minho always makes people laugh.
Dad's joke was so funny.
I take a walk along the river every evening.
We ate fried chicken by the Han River on the weekend.
This river is dangerous for swimming.
Where do they sell this product?

ex.s: 우리 회사 새 제품이 다음 주에 나와요.
ex.en: Our company's new product comes out next week.
Can I get a refund on this product?
My feet hurt from walking so long.
When I get home, I wash my feet first.
What size are your feet?

note: ㅂ irregular: 사랑스러워요.

ex.en: The baby is so adorable.
The puppy looks adorable when it sleeps.
They're a really lovely couple.
I put up a post on my blog.
You write really well.
Take a look at this piece.

note: Polite: 부모님 (use for someone's parents, including your own).

ex.en: Where do your parents live?
I'm going to my parents' place this weekend.
Since becoming a parent, my thinking has changed a lot.

ex.s: 이 상자 좀 같이 옮겨 줄래요?
ex.en: Can you help me move this box?
I'm changing jobs next month.
Can we move to a seat by the window?
My son is in third grade.
What grade are you in?
I went to Korea in my senior year of college.
What's the topic of today's meeting?
Let's talk about a different topic.
That movie's theme was a bit hard to follow.

en: to be old, be a long time
note: As a modifier: 오래된 집 = an old house.

ex.en: This house is really old.
It's been a long time since we've seen each other.
Throw out the old milk.

note: A different verb 적다 means 'to write down'.

ex.en: The portions at this restaurant are a bit small.
There aren't many customers today.
My salary is too low.
There's a school event this weekend.

ex.s: 그 가게에서 할인 행사를 하고 있어요.
ex.en: That store is having a sale.
I'm busy because of a company event.

ex.s: 데이터를 다 써서 인터넷이 안 돼요.
ex.en: I used up all my data, so I can't get online.
There's no Wi-Fi, so I'm using data.
This plan has unlimited data.
This café has a nice atmosphere.
The mood in the meeting wasn't great.
Don't ruin the mood.
This is just between the two of us.
Can you keep a secret?
What's your secret to making it this tasty?

note: 잠시만요 = Just a moment / Excuse me (getting past).

ex.en: Please wait just a moment.
Let's take a short break and then continue.
Excuse me, coming through.

note: 진심으로 = sincerely, from the heart.

ex.en: Thank you from the bottom of my heart.
Do you really mean it?
I'm truly sorry.
Is the water deep here?
You're very thoughtful.
I had a deep conversation with a friend.
How do you express that in Korean?
It's important to express your feelings well.
I showed my gratitude with a gift.

note: 기대돼요 = I'm looking forward to it, I'm excited.

ex.en: I'm really looking forward to the trip.
Don't get your hopes up too much.
I'll be looking forward to my birthday present.
Did you decide what to have for dinner?
Let's set a time to meet.
We haven't decided on the baby's name yet.

note: 결혼하다 = to get married; 결혼식 = wedding ceremony.

ex.en: Congratulations on your wedding!
When did you get married?
We've been married for five years.

note: Usually before a negative: 별 차이 없어요. The noun 별 means 'star'.

ex.en: There's not much difference.
I'm not particularly interested in soccer.
I'm in a good mood for no particular reason.
I have a test tomorrow.
I passed my driving test!
Did you do well on the exam?

note: Casual: 제가 쏠게요 = it's on me.

ex.en: Lunch is on me today.
Minsu treated everyone to coffee for his promotion.
The kids are playing with water guns.
You're always welcome.
Grandma is always smiling.
The roads are always jammed at this time.
What's your goal for this year?

ex.s: 제 목표는 매일 만 보 걷기예요.
ex.en: My goal is to walk 10,000 steps every day.
We beat this month's sales goal.
Do you know the answer?
I texted, but there's no reply yet.
I asked, but he won't answer.

en: to raise, grow; to keep (a pet)

ex.en: Do you have a dog?
I grow tomatoes on the balcony.
She raised two kids on her own.
When does this project end?
I took on a new project.
We're doing a group project at school.
She's a friend from high school.
My daughter starts high school next year.
Which high school did you go to?

note: Follows a place or school: 서울 출신 = from Seoul.

ex.en: Where are you from?
I'm from Chicago.
That teacher went to Seoul National University.

note: ㄹ drops: 푸세요, 푸는.

ex.en: How do you solve this problem?
I relieve stress by working out.
I untied my shoelaces.

note: ㄹ drops: 버세요, 번 돈.

ex.en: I earn money with a part-time job.
I want to make a lot of money.
I'm earning money for a trip.

en: to try hard, make an effort

ex.en: I'll try harder.
I try to get up early every day.
You get out what you put in.
She has a really nice personality.
We really get along.
I'm impatient, so I can't wait long.

note: Polite for another's wife; for your own, say 아내 or 와이프.

ex.en: How is your wife doing?
Mr. Kim's wife is a great cook.
Next time, please come with your wife.
I accepted my friend's apology.
It's not easy to accept your mistakes.
The company accepted my suggestion.

note: 기억이 안 나요 = I can't remember.

ex.en: Do you remember my name?
I can't remember my password.
Do you remember the day we first met?
What novel are you reading these days?
This novel was made into a TV drama.

ex.s: 비행기에서 소설 한 권을 다 읽었어요.
ex.en: I read a whole novel on the plane.
You haven't changed a bit!
The weather suddenly changed.
This neighborhood has changed a lot.
Don't move when I take the picture.
I hurt my leg, so I can't move well.
The car won't move.

note: Casual, to friends or kids; also 너희들. Polite: 여러분. Examples are casual speech.

ex.en: When are you guys arriving?
Your mom is such a good cook.
Kids, did you all finish your homework?
Avoid the morning rush hour.
I'm avoiding coffee these days.
Why do you keep avoiding me?

note: For clothes and shoes, 사이즈 is more common.

ex.en: Do you have this in a smaller size?
The room is just the right size.
Please make the photo a bit smaller.
The machine is broken.
How do you use this machine?
I'm not good with machines.
Choose one of the two.
Why did you choose this school?
You can choose a drink from the menu.

note: 수업을 듣다 = to take a class.

ex.en: What time does class end today?
I take a yoga class every weekend.
I dozed off in class.
What do you usually do on weekends?
I mostly take the subway to work.
I usually eat lunch near the office.

ex.s: 몇 개 언어를 할 수 있어요?
ex.en: How many languages can you speak?
Korean is a really fun language.
Practice is important when learning a language.
We're taking a trip to an island this summer.
Jeju is the biggest island in Korea.

ex.s: 그 섬에 가려면 배를 타야 해요.
ex.en: You have to take a boat to get to that island.
Don't give up!
I already gave up on my diet.
It rained, so we gave up on camping.
I stuck a note on the fridge.
Put a Band-Aid on the cut.
You need to put a stamp on the letter.
I call taxis with this app.
Did you install that app?
The bank app won't open again.

note: 목이 마르다 = to be thirsty.

ex.en: My throat hurts.
I'm thirsty.
My neck is stiff from being on the computer so long.

note: ㄹ drops: 파세요, 파는.

ex.en: Do you sell umbrellas here?
I sold the car I used to drive.
These tickets are only sold online.
Study hard.
I've been working out hard these days.
Everyone worked hard.
My Korean is still at a beginner level.
The food at this restaurant is top quality.

ex.s: 이 수업은 수준이 저한테 좀 높아요.
ex.en: This class is a bit too advanced for me.

note: Homonyms: 연기 can mean acting, smoke, or postponement.

ex.en: That actor is really good at acting.
The acting in this drama is good.
There's smoke coming from the kitchen!

note: 공사 중 = under construction.

ex.en: It's noisy because the house next door is under construction.
This road is blocked because of construction.
When will the subway station construction finish?
My younger sibling is a lawyer.
Try talking to a lawyer.
Lawyer fees are so expensive.

note: 살려 주세요! = Help! (in danger)

ex.en: Help! Save me!
The doctor saved my dad's life.
I brought my dying plant back to life.

note: 참고로 = for reference, just so you know.

ex.en: Just so you know, the store is closed tomorrow.
Please use this material for reference.
Just so you know, I don't eat meat.
My dad reads the newspaper every morning.
These days I read the newspaper on my phone.
Our neighborhood was in the newspaper!

note: For school or college clubs, 동아리 is more common.

ex.en: Are you going clubbing Friday night?
The music at that club is too loud.
I joined a book club.
I walk every day to stay healthy.

ex.s: 멀리 살아도 좋은 관계를 유지하고 있어요.
ex.en: We keep a good relationship even though we live far apart.
I'm maintaining my weight these days.
I ran in a marathon last year.

ex.s: 이 행사는 누구나 참가할 수 있어요.
ex.en: Anyone can take part in this event.
Have you ever entered a cooking contest?
We'll move on to the next place now.
Getting around by subway is faster.
Please move to the meeting room.
We have to consider the price too.
I'm considering moving.
Please take the kids' schedule into account too.
